<thought>Based on the dominant m/z = 183.045 Da peak (likely [M+H]⁺), the neutral mass is ≈182.04 Da. The isotopic pattern suggests about nine carbons. The formula C₉H₁₀O₄ matches this mass closely and is a reasonable candidate for the compound.</thought>
<final_answer>C9H10O4</final_answer>
